**VERDICT: REJECT** **Overall Assessment**: The component fails to provide semantic grouping for a group of related controls and contains a critical functional bug where multiple instances on the same page will merge into a single radio group. It requires `fieldset`/`legend` semantics and dynamic name generation to be accessible and usable. **Pre-commitment Predictions**: 1. Missing `fieldset` and `legend` for grouping context. 2. Static `name` attribute causing DOM collisions when the component is used multiple times. 3. Lack of `role="radiogroup"` on the container. --- ### Critical Findings (blocks access) **1. Radio groups merge into one giant group due to static `name` attribute** * **Evidence**: `src/components/BuggyRadioGroup.jsx:12` (`name="options"`) * **User Group**: Keyboard and Screen Reader users. * **WCAG/APG**: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value; WAI-ARIA APG Radio Button pattern. * **Why this matters**: If a page renders two instances of this component (e.g., one for "Color" and one for "Size"), they share the same `name="options"`. The browser treats all radio buttons with the same name as mutually exclusive options in a single group. Selecting a color will deselect the size option, or vice versa. This is a functional breakage. * **Fix**: Generate a unique `name` string for each instance (e.g., using `crypto.randomUUID()` or a prop) and pass it down: `name={uniqueName}`. **2. Missing semantic grouping (`fieldset`/`legend`)** * **Evidence**: `src/components/BuggyRadioGroup.jsx:7-15` (uses `div` for wrapper and label text). * **User Group**: Screen reader users. * **WCAG/APG**: 1.3.1 Info and Relationships; WAI-ARIA APG Radio Button pattern. * **Why this matters**: Radio buttons are a group of related controls. Without `fieldset` and `legend`, screen readers do not announce the group context (e.g., "Fieldset, Color:"). Users hear a list of radio buttons without knowing what they belong to. The text label is currently just a paragraph (`div`) preceding the inputs. * **Fix**: Wrap the options in `
` and move `{label}` into a ``. **3. Missing `role="radiogroup"` on container** * **Evidence**: `src/components/BuggyRadioGroup.jsx:7` (outer div). * **User Group**: Screen reader users. * **WCAG/APG**: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value. * **Why this matters**: While native `
` provides some grouping context, the WAI-ARIA pattern for a radio group requires `role="radiogroup"` on the container to ensure consistent behavior across all browsers and assistive technologies. * **Fix**: Add `role="radiogroup"` to the wrapper element (or the fieldset). --- ### Major Findings (significantly degrades experience) **1. Label text is not programmatically associated as the group title** * **Evidence**: `src/components/BuggyRadioGroup.jsx:8` (`
{label}
`) * **User Group**: Screen reader users. * **WCAG/APG**: 1.3.1 Info and Relationships. * **Why this matters**: The label text is visually present but structurally disconnected from the radio inputs. It reads as a paragraph before the list, rather than the title of the group. * **Fix**: Use `` inside the `
`. --- ### Minor Findings (friction but workaround exists) **1. Missing `aria-labelledby` on the wrapper** * **Evidence**: `src/components/BuggyRadioGroup.jsx:7` * **Why this matters**: If you cannot use a `legend` (e.g., due to complex layout requirements), the container needs an explicit ID and `aria-labelledby` pointing to it. * **Fix**: Add `id="radio-group-1"` to the wrapper and `aria-labelledby="radio-group-1"`. --- ### What's Missing (gaps) * **Unique ID generation**: The component does not generate unique IDs, leading to the name collision described above. * **`role="radiogroup"`**: The container is a generic `div`. --- ### Multi-Perspective Notes * **Screen reader user**: Will hear "Color" (paragraph), then "Radio button, unchecked". If another group exists on the page, they will hear all radios mixed together in one long list without context. * **Keyboard-only user**: Arrow keys work natively for standard inputs, but if multiple groups exist, arrow keys will navigate across *all* groups instead of just the current one. --- ### Verdict Justification The component is rejected because it contains a critical functional bug (static `name` attribute) that breaks radio group logic when the component is used more than once on a page. Additionally, it lacks the semantic structure (`fieldset`/`legend`) required to communicate the grouping relationship to assistive technology users. --- ### Open Questions (unscored) * Does the parent component handle the `name` collision? (Unlikely given the prop interface). * Is there a requirement for visual-only styling that prevents using `
`? (If so, `role="radiogroup"` is mandatory).
